Vermlings that rise above their baser instincts find that there is much to be gained in exerting their will over beasts of the wilds. These Beast Tyrants can amass incredible armies of fangs, claws and talons to become formidible opponents in battle.
- <indent=%15>Starts with strong Bear ally</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Combines well with all allied summons</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Wide array of multi-use abilities</indent>
- <indent=%15>Weak if Bear is ever exhausted</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Should stay out of melee combat</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Clothes tend to smell a bit 'meaty'</indent>

Berserkers are Inox warriors who have embraced their strength and fury. The Berserker will go to any lengths to keep her friends safe, including sacrificing her own life. Her abilities revolve around high damage output with the option of self-damage to push to even higher amounts. This makes her an extremely dangerous combatant, both to her enemies and herself.
- <indent=%15>One of the highest damage-dealing classes</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Gets even stronger on lower health</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Can lead the front line and draw enemy fire</indent>
- <indent=%15>Little in the way of abilities that help allies</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Operating on low health can lead to premature demise</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Has anger management issues</indent>

The Brute employs his great size and strength to earn a living by wielding his huge sword and impressive shield for those who pay the most.\nBrutes are best used as front line melee troops, absorbing damage and protecting the more fragile ranged damage dealers, and are best equipped with items that keep them alive longer!
The Brute employs his great size and strength to earn a living by wielding his huge sword and impressive shield for those who pay the most.

- <indent=%15>High health and defensive abilities make him more durable than some</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Access to early Disarm and Stun</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Great at pushing enemies about</indent>
- <indent=%15>Low mobility</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Poor ranged attack options</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Not the greatest conversationalist</indent>

Craghearts are Savvas who were exiled for being incapable of mastering an element. Their core is shattered to mark them for life.\nThey have a wide range of abilities and reasonable health meaning they can be used in a defensive melee role, as a ranged damage dealer or even a healer in a pinch. Prioritise using Earth Mana to get the most out of their abilities.
Craghearts are Savvas who were exiled for being incapable of mastering an element. Their core is shattered to mark them for life.

- <indent=%15>Can place and interact with obstacles</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Versatile with melee & ranged options</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Lots of direct damage abilities to dodge Shield and Disadvantage</indent>

- <indent=%15>Doesn't quite excel in any one aspect</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Some abilities require obstacles in specific locations to function</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Hard-to-read facial expressions</indent>

Even when augmenting themselves with machines of their own creation to destroy anything that stands in their path, Quatryls will still do it with charm and flair. Though they may be small, Demolitionists don't let that hold them back in the least. Between their rocket boots, multitude of bombs, and giant piston fists, they are a force to be reckoned with. Sometimes the only path forward is the one they create themselves. In such cases, it is best to get out of their way.
- <indent=%15>Many Direct Damage abilities to smash through Shields</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Access to Abilities with STUN</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Great at affecting the combat area</indent>
- <indent=%15>Small deck size</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Limited healing options</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Their gloves aren't the most practical everyday attire</indent>

Orchid Doomstalkers are tasked with keeping various Orchid settlements safe in the wilds around Gloomhaven. The calm mind of the Orchid makes the Doomstalker an excellent bow hunter. He never misses a shot.
- <indent=%15>High ranged damage</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Doom abilities allow wide array of secondary effects </indent>\n- <indent=%15>Decent array of summons</indent>

- <indent=%15>Generally wants to focus on one enemy at a time</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Casting a Doom often involves skipping movement</indent>\n- <indent=%15>Every visit to Gloomhaven ends up with some poor merchant getting Doomed over the price of an item</indent>

Elementalists are particularly skilled Savvas who have gained mastery of multiple elements. They are respected above others, and can wield powerful magic.\nA complicated class with a lot of complicated abilities, the Elementalist generates and consumes elements at an alarming rate. They work well with other magic users, but if the lone element user in a team, they can be underpowered, best equip them with a way to generate elements if possible.

You find the Beast Tyrant where you always find him: at the bear. It is sitting on its haunches at the edge of the lumber yard, as it has every evening of the campaign, pretending not to watch the crews. The crews pretend not to be watched. It is a comfortable arrangement and it is about to end.
"The wild is going back to being wild," the Vermling says. "Up past the pass, where the Algox do not go. The bear wants it. I have never once told the bear no." He scratches the enormous head, which leans into his hand with the whole of its weight. "I am not starting now."
He leaves you his collection of totems, the wind one and the spirit banner, and a short list of which animals in the valley are to be left alone, in an order that suggests the animals wrote it.
They go at dusk, the man and the bear and a loose tide of smaller things in the undergrowth around them. The lumber yard is quiet for a week. Then the crews start leaving a cut of the day's catch at the edge of the trees, and nobody admits to it.

“There were fifty of them, I swear. Tearing my mates apart!”

You look over to the bar where a group of drunkards are all laughing at a disheveled man in the middle of a story.

“And commanding them all, riding atop a giant armored bear, there was a Vermling with a staff that shot lightning!”

At this the crowd erupts into more laughter, drowning out the rest of the man’s story. “This man’s had too much to drink, I’d say,” ridicules one of the crowd. “Vermlings riding bears! I thought I’d heard of everything!”
Join the crowd in laughing at the man.
You move closer and join in on the fun. After a while, the man gives up and resigns himself to his glass. But his story provides entertainment for weeks.
Calm down the crowd and get more details from the man about the attack.

It’s not easy, but you quiet down the crowd and take the staggering man over to a secluded corner of the tavern to get the full story out of him. Apparently he was part of a group of ruffians working to harvest the Dagger Forest for wood. In the middle of their logging expedition, however, they were attacked by the Beast Tyrant and an army of forest animals. Though he ran off in the middle of the fight, the man swears he also heard the howl of angry spirits in the chaos.

Despite your best efforts, you find yourself lost in a forest. You thought you were taking a shortcut, but then you got turned around and lost your bearings.

And just when you think things couldn’t get worse, a wolf suddenly jumps out of the brush in front of you. Oddly, though, it doesn’t appear aggressive. 

It howls once and then slowly and deliberately begins to walk through the trees in front of you, as if expecting you to follow it.

Miraculously, following the wolf leads you right to the edge of the forest and back on track to your destination. The wolf howls once more and then bounds off back into the brush. You can’t help but wonder who might have sent that wolf to assist you.
Find your own way through the forest.

Not willing to trust a wild animal, you refuse to go in the same direction as the wolf and continue down an ill-fated path of your own choosing. It doesn’t go well, and by the time you emerge from the dense forest and find your bearings, you are exhausted.

Vermlings that rise above their baser instincts find that there is much to be gained in exerting their will over beasts of the wilds. These Beast Tyrants can amass incredible armies of fangs, claws and talons to become formidible opponents in battle.

Role: Melee Damage/Summoner Difficulty: Medium You fight alongside your bear. It joins you at the start of every scenario, and many of your cards command it to , , heal or roar. Keep it alive, since much of your power comes through it. You can summon more animals and spirits, and give your summons , and attack bonuses. Your own attacks are small and ranged, adding , or . You can heal your allies. and boost a few cards. Strengths: • Starts with strong Bear ally • Combines well with all allied summons • Wide array of multi-use abilities Weaknesses: • Weak if Bear is ever exhausted • Should stay out of melee combat • Clothes tend to smell a bit 'meaty'
Lose at least one hit point during each of your turns, without ever performing the bottom action of Blood Pact
Have exactly one hit point at the end of each of your turns

The Berserker is in the Tavern, which is not news, and she is sober, which is. There is a bandage on her arm and a letter on the table in front of her, read so many times the folds have gone soft.
"My sister," she says, pushing it toward you. "The clan is moving the herds south before the snows. She asks if the one who ran off to get herself killed would like to come home instead." She takes the letter back before you can finish it. "She has a way with words."
You ask about the arm. She shrugs: it will heal, they always do, that was never the problem. The problem was that for a long time she did not mind whether they did. "Not any more," she says, and looks surprised to hear it out loud.
She leaves the next morning with the trade caravan, walking beside the wagons rather than riding, because sitting still was never going to happen. At the bend in the road she turns and raises the bandaged arm, once, and then she is gone into the white.

Walking near the northern gates, you see some commotion as a group of wounded guards is ushered into town.

They look pretty bad off, suffering from many severe wounds. Some even have lost limbs.

Bringing up the rear, one guard is carried in by a couple of others. He’s missing a leg and has a vicious-looking axe embedded in his side. You realize that the axe looks kind of familiar.
Let the guards know you recognize the Berserker’s axe.

You approach the wounded detail, explaining how that axe belonged to a former member of your party.\n\n“Yeah, we know,” one of them says with an icy stare. “Said we were desecrating her land or some such nonsense and just went crazy. But we weren’t doing anything but patrolling! Quite a piece of work your friend. Just take the axe if you want and get out of here.”
Stay silent and keep out of it.
You casually move on, wondering how the guards found themselves on the wrong side of the Berserker’s rage. It probably wasn’t very difficult.

You hear the distinctive sound of metal-on-metal in the distance and race up a hill in the road to investigate.\n\nIn front of you, you see a familiar female Inox in heated battle with a group of Gloomhaven guards. Though outnumbered and bloodied, you’ve never seen that stop the Berserker before. With every wound they inflict, she becomes more and more enraged, cleaving off limbs with the ease of cutting grass.
Help the Berserker fight off the guards.

You enter the battle to aid the Berserker, but in her blood rage, she can’t distinguish friend from foe. She begins hacking away at you with her axe as much as she swings at the guards. You concentrate on taking out the remaining guards, but when you turn back to the Berserker, she seems to have vanished into the nearby forest.
Wait and see what happens. It looks like she's handling herself well enough.

After a brutal and bloody fight, only the Berserker remains standing. After her blood rage subsides, she collapses from exhaustion. You race to her side and attempt to revive her using a number of powerful potions. She finally awakes and expresses her begrudging gratitude. You ask about the fight, but she just shakes her head. She offers her axe as thanks and then dashes off into the forest.

Berserkers are Inox warriors who have embraced their strength and fury. The Berserker will go to any lengths to keep her friends safe, including sacrificing her own life. Her abilities revolve around high damage output with the option of self-damage to push to even higher amounts. This makes her an extremely dangerous combatant, both to her enemies and herself.

Role: Melee Damage Difficulty: High Your health is a resource, not just a lifeline. Many of your attacks get stronger the more health you have lost, or once you drop below half, and several cards let you suffer a little damage to make an attack hit harder. Your defences are built for living on the edge: Defiance of Death softens a blow that would knock you out, and other cards boost the healing you receive or strike back whenever you are hurt. Keep a healer close, or plan your own heals. powers some of your attacks, and your blows often add . Strengths: • One of the highest damage-dealing classes • Gets even stronger on lower health • Can lead the front line and draw enemy fire Weaknesses: • Little in the way of abilities that help allies • Operating on low health can lead to premature demise • Has anger management issues
Rested and Ready: +1 <sprite name=Move> to your next move ability
Cause enemies to suffer a total of at least <sprite name=Damage> 12 from retaliate during attacks targeting you in a single round
Across three consecutive rounds, play six different ability cards and cause enemies to suffer at least <sprite name=Damage> 6 on each of your turns

You find the Brute at the main gate at dawn, pack strapped on and shield across his back. He has been quieter than usual these past weeks, which for the Brute is saying something.
"Job's done," he says when you ask. "Came north for the pay. Stayed for..." He gestures at the wall, the gate, the people hauling lumber behind you, and leaves it at that.
He unslings the shield and props it against the gatehouse. "Guard can use it more than I can." A long pause. "Nothing wrong with a wall that holds."
You ask where he will go. He shrugs toward the south: the Frozen Pass, and past it a long walk home to the Great Grove, or to Gloomhaven, or wherever the next quiet place is. You point out he has never been good at quiet. For the first time you can remember, the Brute laughs.
He walks out through the gate without looking back. Behind you, the guards take turns trying to lift the shield.

Walking near the outpost gate, you are approached by a scrawny kid in a guard uniform, which is clearly too big for his small frame.

“Hey, you all are famous!” he says with a big smile. “I worked as a caravan guard before I got this job. Met with a big Inox guy who always talked about you. He made you seem like the nicest, most amazing people.”

His smile and excitement don’t waver. “Say, my detail is doing some work to repair the wall damage from the last attack. Would you mind helping us? It’ll be fun!”
Agree to help the presumptuous kid.

It’s hard work, but the kid’s enthusiasm is infectious. He wants to know all about your exploits and adventures, and he and his detail prove to be a great audience. By the end of the day, it hardly feels like you’ve worked at all.
Tell this kid that he must have the wrong group of adventurers.
You shake your head and avert your gaze. You claim that the kid must have you confused with a different adventuring party. He looks crushed as you walk away.

A trade caravan passes by you on the road. This event isn’t too uncommon, but what catches your eye is a familiar-looking Inox traveling with the caravan as a guard.

At the sight of you, the Brute lights up and gives you a big wave, then rushes over to greet you. He is positively joyful to see you and immediately starts to reminisce about all the exciting battles you fought together.

Slapping you on the back, he implores you to travel with the caravan for a while to give you all a chance to catch up.
Agree to travel with the Brute for a little while. So what if it’s in the wrong direction?

As you walk with the Brute and talk with him about your early adventuring days, you find a hint of sadness behind his enthusiasm. He explains how he fell on hard times after leaving the group and had to resort to jobs like this to make ends meet. The Brute seems uplifted by your conversation, but the day grows late. By the time you head back and arrive at your destination, you are incredibly tired.
Regretfully leave the Brute to his duties and continue on your way.

You explain to the Brute that you have a long day’s travel ahead of you and cannot take the time to travel in the other direction. As you make your good-byes, a shadow falls over him. He walks away forlorn.

You see smoke on the horizon and sigh, expecting the worst. Sure enough, you approach the scene to find a ransacked caravan—burned, pillaged, and destroyed by what appears to be raiders.

You find one survivor among the victims who laments that when the raiders came upon them, one of the guards, a large Inox, seemed to throw aside his weapon and simply accept his fate.

That’s when you find the body of the Brute, torn and bloody among the wreckage. Seeing him this way, the fire gone from his eyes, he appears unnaturally small.
Respectfully bury the dead and mourn their loss.

Though you didn’t take the time to talk with the Brute earlier, now you take the time to bury his corpse and say a few words about his strength of body and character. The survivor thanks you for your help, and you continue on your way once more.
Take what you can find and move on.
Near the corpse of the Brute, you find an axe, presumably the weapon he threw away. There’s really nothing else among the debris, so you wordlessly pick it up and move on.

Role: Melee Damage/Tank Difficulty: Low You are at your best in the middle of a crowd. Many of your attacks hit every adjacent enemy or sweep through an area, so move in where several enemies stand together and hit them all at once. Your hits can , , , and , and a few cards kill a normal enemy outright. Your bottom actions are mostly moves that attack along the way, like Balanced Measure, which turns movement into damage. You have plenty of health, and round-long and to hold the line, so you can afford to take the first hit for your party. Strengths: • High health and defensive abilities make him more durable than some • Access to early Disarm and Stun • Great at pushing enemies about Weaknesses: • Low mobility • Poor ranged attack options • Not the greatest conversationalist
Only attack enemies adjacent to obstacles or walls
Damage or heal at least one ally each round

The Cragheart has been sitting on the same boulder outside the north wall for three days. Nobody thought much of it; the Savvas sits still the way other people breathe. On the fourth morning the boulder is gone, and so is a long stretch of the rubble that the last attack left along the palisade. In its place stands a wall: raw, ugly, and a good deal thicker than the old one.
"It was in the way," the Cragheart says when you find them at the gate, as if that explains the week of work. They have never wasted a word on anything a stone could say for them.
They are going back to the mountains, they tell you, slowly, the way they say everything. Not to the Savvas, who would not have them, but to the high country past the Frozen Pass, where the rock is older and quieter and nobody asks it to fight.
They lay a hand flat against the new wall before they leave, as if listening. Whatever it says satisfies them. The Cragheart walks north, and the ground under the gate does not shake once.

Anticipating an enjoyable night of drinks at the Sleeping Lion, you enter the tavern to see a familiar Savvas sitting at your usual table. The Cragheart stands and extends both its arms.\n\n“Ah, friends! So good to see you,” it says. “Sit! Have a drink with me!”
Have a drink with the Cragheart.

One drink turns into five, and five turns into even more. It is a great night of revelry at the Sleeping Lion. You see sadness in the Cragheart’s eyes when you finally stand up to leave. It tells you it’s been hard to find people to relate to since leaving the party and it thanks you for your continued friendship.
Encourage the Cragheart to move on with its life.

Not fitting in with its own kind or with a city of mostly humans, the Cragheart thought it could depend on a misfit group of mercenaries for friendship. It understands that its adventuring life is now in the past, though, and that it should go find a new place to belong. It sadly admits that it has no idea where that would be, but the Cragheart gets up and leaves the tavern nonetheless.

Walking among the foothills, you see a steep ridge in front of you, and on top of it, a very odd rock formation.\n\nThe formation calls to you somehow, but the way up is not readily apparent. In fact, climbing the ridge looks pretty dangerous, but you just feel like you need to get up there and look at the rocks.
Take the risk to climb to the ridge and investigate the rocks.

Fearing the possibility of falling from a great height, you choose your steps carefully. Still, the climb to the top takes a long time and is exhausting. Reaching the top, you approach the unnatural rock formation, a giant mound of stones stacked one on top of another. At the base of the bottom stone, you see some strange runes and a small pile of gold.
Forget about the rocks and continue on your journey.

You shake your head and move past the ridge. You have more important things to do than climb rocks. Still, you feel the pull of the site, even after it fades from view. You get the feeling that this won’t be the last time you see it.

Role: Damage/Support Difficulty: Medium You shape the battlefield with rock. Many of your cards create obstacles, destroy them for extra effects, or push enemies into them for more damage. Rock Slide drops boulders that hurt everyone standing next to them. powers your bigger attacks, extra movement and . Many of your attacks hit several enemies at once, often in large areas. Be careful: several of your abilities also damage allies standing next to you, so warn your party before you use them. You are tough, jump well, and have a little healing for yourself and your friends. Strengths: • Can place and interact with obstacles • Versatile with melee & ranged options • Lots of direct damage abilities to dodge Shield and Disadvantage Weaknesses: • Doesn't quite excel in any one aspect • Some abilities require obstacles in specific locations to function • Hard-to-read facial expressions
Deal <sprite name=Damage> 10 or more with each of three different attack actions
Destroy at least six obstacles. End the scenario with no obstacles on the map other than ones placed by allies

The explosion wakes the whole outpost an hour before dawn. By the time you reach the harbor the Demolitionist is standing on the ice, or what is left of it, surrounded by delighted fishermen. The channel that has been frozen shut since midwinter is open water.
"You said the boats could not get out," she says, as if that settled it. The rocket boots are smoking gently. The mech suit stands on the quay behind her like a patient dog.
The foreman from the mine has been watching from the harbor wall. He has a seam that will not open and a crew that is tired of picks, and he offers her the job before the ice has stopped moving. She considers it for as long as it takes to reload. "Things that need breaking," she says. "I can do that."
She takes the suit up the mountain road the next day, the fists folded, the whole contraption leaving prints like a bear in the snow. Twice a week, for years afterwards, a dull thump rolls down from the mine, and the whole of Frosthaven looks up and smiles.

Even when augmenting themselves with machines of their own creation to destroy anything that stands in their path, Quatryls will still do it with charm and flair. Though they may be small, Demolitionists don't let that hold them back in the least. Between their rocket boots, multitude of bombs, and giant piston fists, they are a force to be reckoned with. Sometimes the only path forward is the one they create themselves. In such cases, it is best to get out of their way.

Role: Melee Damage Difficulty: Medium Walls and obstacles are your playground. Many of your cards destroy obstacles, and each destruction pays off with damage, , or . Enemies standing next to a wall also take extra damage from several of your attacks. At level 5 you gain the Mech Suit, a lasting transformation: you change shape, gain extra health and a shield, and recover cards. and add damage, , and pushes. Your attacks are mostly up close, and some can . Strengths: • Many Direct Damage abilities to smash through Shields • Access to Abilities with STUN • Great at affecting the combat area Weaknesses: • Small deck size • Limited healing options • Their gloves aren't the most practical everyday attire
Never perform a Doom action that you have already performed in the scenario
Kill three Doomed enemies during one of your turns

The Doomstalker has not spoken more than a sentence a week since he arrived, so when he asks you to walk the north ridge with him at dawn, you go. He says nothing for an hour. Then he points, and you see the tracks you have walked past a hundred times: something large, keeping its distance, watching the outpost as patiently as he has.
"I have marked it," he says. You do not ask what that means. You have seen what happens to things he marks.
He leaves the bow with the guard captain, strung, with a single arrow laid beside it, and the captain understands the arrangement without being told: the day the thing on the ridge comes closer, there is one shot, and it will not miss. It never comes closer.
He goes north himself, after it or past it, with his animals ranging ahead of him in a loose silent fan. For years after, the hunters swear the valley's wolves give the outpost a wider berth than any other place on the pass, and nobody can tell them why.

“Ah, they said I might find you here.” A portly Valrath woman looks down at you as you are enjoying a cold beverage at the Sleeping Lion.

“A group of wild-looking Orchids came to the Temple of Coin today hoping to engage in trade with the merchants of the city. One particularly dour-looking one with a bow said you lot would vouch for them.

“We’re always wary of traps and betrayal out here on the edge of the wilds, but if you think these Orchids can be trusted, then the Merchant’s Guild may consider opening trade with them.”

“Well, we’ll take it under advisement. Personally, I don’t even know why your opinion matters, but some people in the Merchant’s Guild seem to like you.\n\n“Anyway, feel free to get back to your life of consumption and murder.”
Advise against trading with the Orchids.
The Valrath woman nods. “I agree. Orchids are not to be trusted. Personally, I thought you lacked the brains to make a proper decision, but I’m happy to be proven wrong.”

You come to a fork in the road. One path looks clear and easy, but the other path is overgrown with thorns and nettles. Either one will likely get you to where you are going.

The whole situation feels off, though—as if someone or something is watching you.

Still, a decision must be made.

You walk down the clear path for a few minutes, and, just when you think the whole weird feeling was your imagination, a group of human bandits jumps out at you from the nearby brush. Before they can engage, however, an arrow suddenly spears the chest of the closest bandit, followed very quickly by a second. The bandits have paused to look around in panic when a third arrow flies into another bandit’s skull. The bandits scatter and run off. You look around for the shooter, but no trace is found.

The trek through the overgrown path is unpleasant. You are constantly getting pricked by sharp thorns covered in a strange sap. You think you recognize them from a previous foray into harsh, unforgiving foliage. Sure enough, you start feeling sick pretty soon after you emerge from the bushes.

Orchid Doomstalkers are tasked with keeping various Orchid settlements safe in the wilds around Gloomhaven. The calm mind of the Orchid makes the Doomstalker an excellent bow hunter. He never misses a shot.

Role: Ranged Damage/Support Difficulty: Medium You place dooms on enemies. A doom is a lasting mark that stays on its target: your attacks against it are stronger, and when the doomed enemy dies, the doom pays off with healing, damage around it, or another effect. You can normally keep one doom out at a time. You are an archer who fights from far away, and several attacks hit harder against a doomed target. Expose gives you advantage against it. You can summon animal companions and set bear traps. Your own attacks rarely add conditions: your dooms do that work. Strengths: • High ranged damage • Doom abilities allow wide array of secondary effects • Decent array of summons Weaknesses: • Generally wants to focus on one enemy at a time • Casting a Doom often involves skipping movement • Every visit to Gloomhaven ends up with some poor merchant getting Doomed over the price of an item
Consume at least two different elements with each of four different attack abilities, without ever performing the bottom action of Formless Power or Shaping the Ether
Infuse five or more elements during one of your turns, then consume five or more elements during your following turn

The Elementalist calls it balancing the ledger. Six elements, drawn and spent and drawn again over a winter of fighting, and the Savvas keep count of such things the way merchants keep count of coin. "I have taken more fire from this valley than I gave it," they say, standing at the frozen edge of the bay. "That is not a thing to leave behind."
So they give it back. For a week the outpost is warmer than it has any right to be in that season: the ice in the harbour rots, the lumber yard's frozen stack comes loose with a sound like a sigh, and the Infirmary's patients sleep without blankets for the first time since autumn.
Then the Elementalist takes the cold instead, folds it into themself with the same unhurried care, and walks north into the white with it, toward wherever a Savvas goes to be respected. They do not say goodbye. They have never seen the point.
The thaw they left lasts exactly as long as they said it would, to the day. Frosthaven learns to plan around it, and nobody ever quite believes it was weather.

You are haggling over the price of road rations with an irritating Valrath merchant when a messenger boy approaches you holding a note.

“Sir, I have a pressing letter written by a powerful Savvas that has come to you from all the way across the Misty Sea,” the messenger says. “I was told to deliver it directly.”

You reach for it, but the messenger moves back a little. “Sir, this note has traveled a very long distance to get to you. If you could, please pay a small fee to take possession of it.”
You reach into your pocket to pay the kid, but come up empty-handed. He slinks off in indignation.
Refuse to pay for the note.

You laugh in indignation and push the messenger away. He opens his mouth to object, then thinks better of it and runs off. You turn back to bartering, now leveraging the proof of your extreme thriftiness against the merchant.

You are wandering through an abysmal fog, cursing the very fact you woke up this morning. You can’t see two feet in front of your face and everything is just so cold and damp.

Walking down what you think is the road, you nearly bump into an elderly Savvas.

“Ah, how fortuitous is such a meeting,” the Savvas says. “You look like the ones whom my protégé worked with for some time. Normally I would not give the lesser races a second glance, but the master of elements must have seen something in you.”

It stretches its joints and looks around. “Hmm, you must be having a rough time with this weather. I could offer you something that may help.”
Accept the gift of the Savvas.

The Savvas concentrates and lays its hand on you. You suddenly feel very warm and all the fog within ten feet of you dissipates.\n\n“There you go. That should make things easier. The effect should last for at least as long as the fog does. Have a pleasant day!”
Downplay your struggle and politely decline the Savvas's offer.

“Ah, I see,” the Savvas says. “You’d rather grow from an experience than take the easy way out. A noble path.”\n\nThe Savvas slaps you on the back. “Well, get to it, then! It’s just fog after all. You’ll survive."

As you walk through some foothills, the ground suddenly shakes violently beneath you. Two massive demons built of earth and stone rise up in front of you.

“Today we shall feast on your flesh, foolish travelers!”

Just as the demons take a step toward you, a massive ball of fire streaks through the air from behind and connects squarely with one of the demons, which erupts into a pillar of flame. Then lightning streaks toward the other, destroying one of its arms.

Looking around, you see the old Savvas you met earlier, who continues to throw out powerful attacks until the demons are forced to retreat.

“Well, fancy meeting you again!”
Thank the Savvas for his timely assistance.

“More and more demons around these parts these days. Stopping them from attacking travelers is becoming a time-intensive job, but at least it’s fun.”\n\nThe Savvas smiles at you and then turns to leave. “Have a pleasant day!”
Admonish the Savvas, claiming you could have handled the demons without his help.

The Savvas adopts a look of serious contemplation. “You are right, of course. I presumed to think that a lesser race would need my help, but I forgot your dedication to growth and learning. I have made a grave mistake and must now beg your forgiveness.”\n\nIt holds out a small trinket toward you. “Please, accept this with my apologies.”

Role: Ranged Damage Difficulty: Very High Almost every one of your abilities changes with the element you spend. The same attack can push, stun, pierce or hit harder depending on whether you spend , , , or . Plan your turns around which elements are strong, and make the ones you need. Formless Power lets you create an element of your choice at the end of each turn. Without elements your attacks are weak, so keep them flowing. You can also heal and shield your allies, and summon helpers. Strengths: • Abilities have wide array of options • Very effective at range • Great at infusing elements Weaknesses: • Weak with no other element infusers • Can have turns where not much is possible • Reading his ability cards can cause migraines
Throw or recover the Favorite during each of your turns
During each round in which there is at least one enemy on the map at the start of your turn, throw the Favorite at an enemy or return it to your ability card

The Hatchet has a new coat. It is dark green, cut in the Capital style, and entirely wrong for Frosthaven, which he knows perfectly well. He wears it to the gate anyway, the Favorite hanging at his hip where the fashion says a sword should go.
"A troupe is going south with the caravan," he says. "Knife throwers, fire eaters, that sort of thing. They lost their axe man in a tavern in the Capital. I told them I could be worse." He grins, which the coat was clearly bought for. "Nobody in a crowd ever throws back. I could get used to that."
He looks at the wall for a moment, the way everyone does before they go, then pulls the Favorite and throws it. It buries itself in the gatepost at head height, a hair from the guard's ear. The guard does not flinch; the Hatchet taught him not to, over a long winter of exactly this.
He walks over, works the axe free, kisses the blade, and goes. The notch stays in the post. New recruits are told to stand with their heads against it, and never told why.

While any normal Inox may be valued in Gloomhaven for their brute strength and endurance with manual labour, if you want to be a successful mercenary in the city, sometimes a little more finesse is required. Hatchets have fully embraced life in the city, outfitting themselves in the latest fashions. It is all a bit of a front though, as their true passion lies in their arsenal. No one is a better marksman with a throwing axe, and if anybody wants to challenge their claim, they had better be prepared for a duel to the death!

Role: Ranged Damage Difficulty: Low Your signature is The Favorite, your best axe. Some attacks throw it at an enemy, where it stays: your attacks against that enemy are stronger while it carries the axe, and a few cards let you take it back. You fight from range, throwing axes at 3 or 4 hexes. extends your range and adds pushes, extra movement or a second attack. Killing an enemy fuels your next moves: several cards give you extra movement, healing or after a kill. Your attacks can also , and you have good loot. Strengths: • Great Ranged Damage • Reasonable array of varied secondary abilities • Has a couple of Favourite Axes Weaknesses: • Should try and keep out of the front line • Needs to go pick his axes up after use • Hasn't been able to remove their hat since childhood
Trigger the on-attack effect of four different Augments thrice each
Never be targeted by an attack

The rats go first. For three days the outpost's granary is quieter than anyone can remember, and the Craftsman, who has fought the vermin for years, walks around looking cheated. Then the Mindthief comes to find you, a swarm's worth of small warm bodies gone from the folds of her cloak, and tells you she has sent them ahead.
"There is a nest in the Copperneck," she says, "a big one. They have been talking about it for a month." You ask who. She looks at you the way she looks at anyone who asks a question she has already answered in their head. "The rats."
She leaves you her blade, the thin wicked one, and with it a thought she presses into you so firmly that you still feel it years later whenever you draw it: nothing in front of you is as dangerous as what is behind it. You have never been sure whether it was advice or a joke at your expense.
By the time the Craftsman has finished celebrating, every rat in Frosthaven is back, and the granary is exactly as it was. The Mindthief is not.

Walking near Gloomhaven Square, you see a peculiar scene. A group of guards is dragging along a Vermling in tattered robes toward the Ghost Fortress. Getting a little closer, you
recognize the Mindthief.

“Hssss,” she spits. “Why do you do this? I came to you! I tell you that this town is being poisoned, and you respond by imprisoning me?”

“We’ll see what the Captain of the Guard has to say about this,” one of her captors says. “Keep moving!”
Intervene with the guards and find out what is going on.

The guards look incredibly perturbed when you step in front of them and ask that they leave the Mindthief to you. After some effort, they begrudgingly hand her over. The Mindthief thanks you, explaining that her colony in the sewers is being poisoned, and the poison is quickly migrating to the city’s water supply. She says she’s tracked the source to a small cove along the Hook Coast.
Let the guards continue their business and just continue with yours.

The Mindthief flicks her tail and throws insults around, but it doesn’t seem to have any positive effect. She is led away and out of view. You get about your business, hoping that bit about the town being poisoned wasn’t too serious.

A single Vermling jumps out of the brush at you, surprising you briefly. Within moments, though, you have your weapons out and pressed against his throat.

“EEEEEEEeeeahh!” The Vermling drops his weapon and cowers. “No attack! My brothers in the bushes say you had stink of city-dwelling outcast on you. I wanted to be sure.”

The Vermling waves his hands. “It’s not bad! Just curious. Being stinky city-dwelling outcast is fine. Please, don’t hurt me!”
Move on, leave the strange Vermling in peace.
“Stink very faint,” the Vermling continues as you walk on. “Outcast no longer with you, but I still smell it!”\n\nHe then jumps back into the brush. Vermlings are very odd creatures.

You attack the Vermling anyway, despite his protests. It turns out he wasn’t lying about his “brothers” nearby, though. As you wipe the blood from your blade, ten more of the little furry creatures jump out at you, brandishing small knives. They are not nearly as easy to dispatch.

“I assume you are aware of an increased amount of sickness in the city.”

You were summoned to the Ghost Fortress and now stand before the Captain of the Guard.

“We believe it could have something to do with a poisoning threat brought to our attention by your Mindthief friend a while ago. We ignored it, but now she is nowhere to be found, the Hook Coast is a bed of disease, and Gloomhaven proper is on its way there, too.”

He looks at you firmly. “I need you to head down to the Hook Coast and figure out what is going on. Then eliminate the source of the poison."

The Hook Coast is outside the walls of Gloomhaven and can be a dangerous place. And since this spread of poison, the city has become even more defenseless than normal. You hope you’ll be able to find a solution to the problem quickly.
Tell the captain to fix his own problem.

The Captain of the Guard sighs.

“I really thought you were the ones for the job. What business could you possibly have that is more important than making sure this city is safe?”

He holds up his hand. “No matter. Fine, just get out of here! We will deal with this ourselves.”

Role: Melee Damage Difficulty: High You use augments: lasting cards that add an effect to every melee attack you make, such as extra damage, healing, , or . Only a limited number can be active at once, so choose the ones that suit the fight. Your other strength is control. Several cards make an enemy attack itself or its neighbour, or move where you want it, and a few let you command an ally. Your attacks hit harder against enemies with negative conditions. and add stuns and extra attacks. You move fast and can summon rats, but you are fragile. Strengths: • Powerful Augment effects on melee attacks • Mind-control powers • Access to summons Weaknesses: • Fragile melee character • Managing Augments can be fiddly • Often confused for a giant rat
Have <sprite name=Invisible> at the start or end of each of your turns
Infuse or consume <sprite name=CreateDark> during each of your turns

You had agreed to meet the Nightshroud at the Barracks at dusk. You arrive early. He is already there, which you only learn when he speaks from the shadow of the doorway you have been standing in for a minute.
"I am going back," he says. Not to Gloomhaven; back, in the way the Aesther mean it, to whichever fold of the world they step out of and into. He has found the edge of it here, in the long dark of the Frosthaven winter. "It is thin, this far north. I have been half through for weeks."
He hands you his knife, hilt first, the one you have watched end a dozen things before they knew they were in danger. "Keep it in the dark," he says, and for once you cannot tell whether it is advice or a joke.
Then the lamp in the doorway gutters, and when it steadies the shadow is only a shadow. The guards on the wall swear nobody passed them. For the first night in months, nothing in the outpost moves that you did not see.

You are wandering through the city streets late at night when you hear a terrifying scream high above you. You look up just in time to see a body falling toward you and jump out of the way.

It lands with a wet thud on the ground. You were not the only ones to hear the scream, and quickly a small crowd forms around the corpse, including a couple of city guards.

The body is clad in black leather armor, and a long, thin blade conspicuously protrudes from its back. You remark that the sword somehow looks familiar.

“What?” asks a guard. “This is the third murder like this in a week. Tell me everything you know!”
Tell the guard that the sword belongs to the Nightshroud, your former party member.

You explain that you recognize the sword from the time you spent traveling with the Nightshroud. As a capable assassin, he is likely to be the one behind the murders. You explain, however, that since he left the group, you have no knowledge of his whereabouts or dealings. The guard thanks you for the information.
Lie and claim you know nothing.
You laugh and make up some poor explanation about seeing a similar sword on a bandit in a crypt. The guard eyes you suspiciously.

You reach a crossroads and decide to rest for a bit. As you eat some of your rations, something sticking up out of the ground in the distance catches your attention.

You move closer, and what you thought was a signpost turns out to be a human skull impaled on a spike.

There is something sticking out of the skull’s mouth.

You get closer to the pike. The skull looks pretty fresh. There are still bits of decayed flesh attached to the bone, and flies buzz around it. You can see there is a small paper card stuck in its mouth, so you carefully reach in and pull it out. The card is black and depicts a skull with blades running through it. Come to think of it, you remember rumors of an assassins’ guild that has been known to use the same imagery. You get out of the area as quickly as you can.
Arm yourself and make a defensive retreat from the area.

You remember rumors of an assassins’ guild that places a skull on a pike outside the houses of their victims before they strike. Fearing the worst, you pull out your weapons and survey the scene as you back away from the pike. Everything looks clear, so you quickly get as far away from the area as possible. Perhaps the skull was not meant for you.

Late in the evening, you are returning to your rooms when you hear a cry for help coming from a nearby alleyway. Racing into the shadows, you expect to find someone in distress, but instead find a group of men clad in black leather armor eying you maliciously.

“We have a message for your Nightshroud friend,” one of them says, drawing a wicked-looking curved blade. Suddenly, the Nightshroud appears among them in a flash of fatal sword strikes. Before the men even have a chance to react, half of them lie dead on the ground. The other half quickly flee.

“Well, it looks like you’re into it now, too. Which is good, because I need help taking them down.”
Stay and listen to what the Nightshroud has to say.

The Nightshroud kicks one of the corpses. “This is the Sin-Ra Syndicate, a group of assassins trying to gain a foothold in the region. I’m trying to stop them, and somehow they found out you and I were friends. They decided to go after you as retribution. Lucky for you, I’ve located their hideout, so we’re going to sneak in there and end this whole business once and for all.”
Claim you want nothing to do with this and walk away.

“The Sin-Ra Syndicate seems to think you have something to do with this,” the Nightshroud yells at you as you leave. “That’s all that matters! They’ll strike again, and I won’t be there to protect you!” You keep walking.

You reach a crossroads and decide to rest for a bit. As you eat some of your rations, something sticking up out of the ground in the distance catches your attention.

You move closer, and what you thought was a signpost turns out to be a human skull impaled on a spike.

There is something sticking out of the skull’s mouth.

Against your better judgment, you approach the skull, which looks suspiciously like the Sin-Ra’s calling card. Sure enough, a group of dark-clad warriors appears before you from out of thin air. Wordlessly, they draw their long, curved blades and attack. Caught by surprise, you don’t fare well in the battle. You do fight them off, but in the end, you are severely wounded, exhausted, and demoralized.
Arm yourself and make a defensive retreat from the area.

Recognizing the pike as a symbol of the Sin-Ra Syndicate, you arm yourself and run from the area. Unfortunately, you don’t make it far before you see a number of black-clad assassins bearing down on you. You move into a defensive position and prepare for battle. The fight is arduous, but in the end, the assassins are dead, and you hope they don’t come back.

With the ability to cloak themselves in shadow and pass through the world unseen, Nightshrouds are deadly stalkers, using blades and stealth to eliminate any target. Rather than working with other races to gather knowledge, Nightshrouds prefer to pry the knowledge from their cold, dead fingers.

Role: Melee Damage Difficulty: Medium Darkness is your fuel. Most of your cards create or spend it, and spending it is what turns a good turn into a great one. Nightfall keeps Dark flowing every turn, so it is worth getting out early. Your other tool is . Many of your attacks hit harder or add effects while you are unseen, so plan your turns around becoming invisible, striking, and slipping away before enemies can answer. Your attacks can , , and enemies, and a few Dark-fuelled ones, like Spirit of the Night, kill a normal enemy outright. You fight up close and are fairly fragile, so use your long moves and jumps to pick your fights, and avoid crowds while you can be seen. Strengths: • Powerful execution abilities • Can use Invisibility to avoid damage • Uses Dark to enhance his abilities Weaknesses: • Poor ranged options • Doesn't assist allies much • Finds making friends difficult
Kill at least five enemies with non-attack abilities
Perform three different attack abilities that target at least four enemies each

The Alchemist finds you first, which tells you something has gone wrong before she says a word. "Your Harrower friend," she says, "has been in my stillroom all night. I would like them out of it. I would also like to know what they left in the third jar from the end."
You find the Plagueherald on the roof of the Alchemist's, the swarm settled over them like a shawl, watching the sun come up over the bay. They do not turn around. "The jar is a cure," they say. "For the cough the lumber crews have. She will work it out in a month; I have saved her the month."
They are leaving. The hive has decided, they explain, and a Harrower does not argue with the hive. Somewhere warmer, somewhere with more rot to feed on; they say it the way someone else would mention the weather.
The swarm lifts off the roof all at once, a dark sheet that folds and is gone over the water. The cough is gone from the crews by the end of the week. The Alchemist still will not open the third jar.

You have been hearing rumors in the bars: a pox is spreading through Gloomhaven, affecting lower class citizens—street urchins and backalley thugs.

And then one night you see it: a Harrower dressed in a ragged green cloak holding a man down in an alley as its swarm spreads out and consumes him. The man’s screams are muffled as the insects skitter down his throat.

Killing monsters and demons is one thing, but the Plagueherald shouldn’t be preying on people in the city. You approach it, intent on stopping its attack.
Calmly explain the situation to the Plagueherald, imploring it to move on.

With the man dead at its feet, the Plagueherald makes a chittering sound that sounds almost like laughing.

“You cannot see it, but this city needs to be cleansed. You will see, and you will thank me.”

At this, the Plagueherald bursts out into a massive swarm of insects and flies up into the sky.

The deaths continue, and new rumors start about how you are associated with the killer.
Threaten the Plagueherald with retribution if it doesn’t stop attacking residents.

The Plagueherald recoils at your threat, genuinely concerned that you would attack it.

“But, the cleansing...the city isn’t ready.”

You shake your head, and the Harrower chitters in disappointment.

“Very well, but you will be responsible when the Harbinger comes.” It turns and floats off into the darkness.

You smell the corpses before you see them. A group of five or so, spread across the road, flies buzzing around in a frenzy.

As you get closer, you see the wretched, deformed looks on their faces and the boils covering their skin. You also see their crude armor and weapons—likely a group of cutthroats.

What is truly odd, though, is that their weapons are out of their sheaths in the first place. It appears they were engaged in battle when they suddenly succumbed to some horrible disease.

You can think of at least one way that could have happened. Fine handiwork from the Plagueherald.
Knowing better than to get too close to the machinations of the Plagueherald, you keep a wide berth between you and the corpses and continue down the road.
You rifle through the corpses, grabbing stray coins and valuables as you go. You make off with a good haul, but you start feeling sick as soon as you’re done.

Either misguided or ignorant of other races’ physiology, Plagueheralds believe that the spread of disease throughout a society will strengthen it and propel it towards great things. One should be wary of allying with a Plagueherald. Their ability to spread decay and death across both sides of a battlefield is a terrifying thing to behold.

Role: Ranged Damage/Support Difficulty: Medium Sickness is your weapon. You attack from range, often in large clouds, and most of your attacks , , or everything they touch. Spread first, then cash it in: cards like Succumb to the Gift kill a poisoned enemy outright, and others deal damage to every poisoned enemy at once. is your second tool, and powers a few of your strongest effects. You are fragile and have little protection, so keep your distance and let the poison do the work. Strengths: • Can often target multiple enemies • Effective at range • Powerful debuffs utilizing Curse and Poison Weaknesses: • High potential for friendly fire • Low effectiveness versus single large targets • Harrower mating rituals are... unpleasant
Spend, lose or refresh one or more items on each of your turns, without ever performing the top action of Reinforced Steel
Loot six or more loot tokens in a single turn

The Quartermaster spends his last week in Frosthaven doing inventory. Not his own: the outpost's. By the end of it every storeroom has a ledger, every ledger has a system, and the Craftsman has stopped arguing and started taking notes.
"A party without supplies is a funeral with extra steps," he tells you over the last of his good wine. "You lot will be fine. You have the ledgers now." He taps the stack like a man patting a dog.
He has a contract waiting in the Capital, outfitting a merchant house, and he is honest enough to admit the pay is obscene. He is also honest enough to look back at the walls for a long moment before he goes.
His pack is the last thing to leave, strapped to a sled and roped like a siege engine. The Craftsman swears the storerooms have never been so tidy, and never will be again.

“Your Quartermaster friend sent me.” You look quizzically at the Valrath standing at your door.

“I’m from the Capital, and I deal in arms and armor,” he says. “I’m looking to set up a contract with the Frosthaven guard, and our friend says that you may have some contacts with them. He suggested I meet up with you once I got here.”

The Valrath shifts his feet nervously. “So, can you help me?”
Agree to help him make contact with the guard.

You take the Valrath over to the Barracks, where you make introductions to the captain of the guard. The captain seems skeptical at first, but admits that they could use an additional supply of weapons. Terms are made, and a contract is signed.
Demand a finder’s fee for setting him up with buyers.
The Valrath looks at you with trepidation, but after some persuasion, you get him to agree.

You are approached on the road by a group of men on horseback. They don’t immediately seem menacing, but they are formidable and well organized.

One of the men, who wears plate armor and has a sword at his side, addresses you coldly. “You hail from Frosthaven, correct? What say you about the politics of the place? Are you for or against military rule in the region? Do you think those fool merchants could do a better job, like they’re doing with the rest of this doomed land?”

Looking closer, you see all the men wear the signet of a tower with an eye at its center.

The armored men seem satisfied with your response and take their hands off their weapons.\n\n“Good to find some fellow patriots,” the one in front says with a disturbing smile. “You know, we have a stronghold not far from here up in the mountains. Feel free to visit there if you ever get serious about your loyalties.”
Claim allegiance to the merchant guilds.

“Well then, today’s your unlucky day,” the man in front says. “Because we of the Vigil make it a point to execute any and all commerce sympathizers we can find in this land.”\n\nThe men grimly draw swords and advance. After a hard battle, the survivors retreat, leaving you to pick through the corpses. Among the loot you find a map.
Skilled Valrath Quartermasters are known for aiding adventuring parties in maximizing the effectiveness of their equipment. After all, what is a warrior without a good sword at his side?

Role: Melee Damage/Support Difficulty: Medium Items are your resource. Many of your cards refresh spent items, for you or for the whole party, so do not be shy about using them. Proficiency makes your attacks stronger in any action where you used an item. Your weapons are your cards: axe and spear sweeps up close, a bow at range, and one-use scrolls with the biggest effects in your deck. Save those scrolls for the moments that matter, since they are lost once used. You also support the party with and bonuses, healing, and cards that give allies their discarded cards back. Strengths: • Many item refreshing abilities • Moderate offensive and defensive capabilities • Jack of all trades Weaknesses: • Master of none • Weaker when party lacks good equipment • Always packs too much luggage
Kill at least five enemies during their turns
Force each enemy in the scenario to move at least one hex, forcing at least six enemies to move

The Red Guard does not leave. That is the first thing she tells you, before you can ask. She has walked the wall every night since the first attack, in the red armor that marks her as an exile from a city that no longer wants her, and somewhere in all those nights the wall became hers.
"In Jhinda the guard is a caste," she says. "You are born to it or you are not. Here you are a guard because you stand on the wall when it matters. I find I prefer that." The captain of the watch has offered her a post, a bunk in the Barracks and the north tower. She has already moved her things.
She hands you the sickle and chain, the weapon she pulled a hundred enemies off their feet with. "The guard issues a spear. I would hate to be the one who makes an exception."
That night the torch in the north tower stays lit until dawn, and it does every night after. The lumber crews stop asking who is up there. They just stop looking over their shoulders.

There is a specific caste in the Valrath capital of Jhinda tasked with protecting the city. It is a prestigious position and one not easily lived up to. Outcast from Jhinda for unknown crimes, the Red Guard found it too difficult to part from their identity as a protector, keeping the distinctive red armor, as well as their chained sickle and shield. The only place to find work was as a mercenary in Gloomhaven, and maybe, just maybe, by standing on the front lines and keeping their allies from harm, the Red Guard will find some way to redeem themselves. Not in the eyes of the Jhinda culture, which has permanently turned its back, but at least within their own esteem.

Role: Tank Difficulty: Low You hold the front line with shield and sickle. Your sickle attacks reach two hexes and often enemies to you or them, and many cards give you or hurt every enemy standing next to you. You use two elements. adds , larger areas and stronger pulls; adds attack, shields, and extra movement. Keep both flowing. Pull enemies into your reach and keep them busy so your allies do not have to. Strengths: • Array of Melee attacks plus some Ranged • Combination of Shield and direct damage dealing close up • Wide Initiative range enables 'double turns' Weaknesses: • Outside of damage, doesn't have many options • May struggle against single larger enemies • Really, and I mean REALLY, likes the colour Red
On each of your turns, give an ally a card, heal an ally, grant an ally <sprite name=Shield>, or place a card in an ally's active area
Deal at least <sprite name=Damage> 20 with a single attack ability

You find the Sawbones in the Alchemist's back room, labeling jars. He has been at it for days: every salve, splint and tincture he carried, written up in his cramped hand and shelved where anyone can find it.
"Enough people know how to break things in this town," he says without looking up. "Somebody ought to know how to put them back together when I am gone." He closes the last jar, wipes his hands, and finally turns around. "The sanctuary wrote. A quiet post, inland. Warm. I said yes before I could talk myself out of it."
He leaves you his saw. Not as a weapon, he insists, though you both know how he used it. "For the lumber. Honestly."
The morning he goes, half the outpost turns out to see him off, every one of them someone he has stitched, set or sobered up. He pretends to be annoyed about it the whole way to the gate.

Looking for a little bit of variety, you head to the roughest table in the Tavern as night falls. After some wait, you are surprised to see the Sawbones sitting near the back of the room by himself. Considering this corner is about as seedy as Frosthaven gets, it is just about the last place you would expect to find him.

“I just...I don’t know what to do now,” the Sawbones confesses after you sit down. “I’d like to join the sanctuary and lead a nice, quiet life, but after adventuring with all of you, that just doesn’t seem fulfilling anymore.”

He shakes his head. “I don’t know. This life seems so boring now. What do you think?”
Tell him that joining the sanctuary is the right thing to do.
“I guess you’re right,” he shrugs. “Here’s to one last night of freedom.” He lifts his glass and gulps down the contents. You follow his lead and the rest is a blur.
Tell him to follow his dreams.

“You’re right! I’m in command of my own life, and I’m going to do what I want with it. Maybe I’ll go to the Capital and start my own business or something. Who knows?”\n\nHe lifts his glass and looks at you. “To endless possibilities! The next round’s on me.”

At first the man looks dead, with numerous open wounds and lying in a pool of blood in the dirt.\n\nBut then he coughs and whispers something unintelligible. The man looks pretty bad off, likely attacked by some wild animal, but it’s possible he could be saved.
Help the wounded man as best you can.

The man’s wounds actually look worse than they really are, and your time with the Sawbones has given you some experience in what to do. You bind the wounds to stop the bleeding and then give him something to eat. He lost a lot of blood, but after some nursing, he’s able to stand and make his way back to Frosthaven, thanking you profusely in the process.
Let the man die and take his belongings.

You riffle through the man’s pockets as he speaks his last words. They’re too soft to make out, but the tone is one of anger and disappointment. You make off with a decent amount of money and leave the corpse to rot.

You head back to your rooms for the night when you see the Sawbones sitting in front of your doorstep, looking rather dejected.

“I, uh, well, you see...” he stammers, “I followed your advice. Chased my dreams and all that, but I ended up in debt to some rather unscrupulous people. They’ve threatened to kill me if I don’t pay them off, but, uh, but I simply don’t have the money.”

He hesitates. “Seeing as how, uh, you bear some responsibility for setting me down this path, I was wondering if you’d be willing to offer some assistance in getting me out of this mess?”
Offer to pay off the Sawbones’ debt.

It’s a hefty chunk of money, but the Sawbones is incredibly grateful.

“This is wonderful! I knew I could count on you. This should be enough to put this mess behind me and finally allow me to live free.”

He hands you a potion and thanks you once again for all your help.
Get the Sawbones on a boat across the Misty Sea. New adventures surely await there.

You flatly refuse to pay off the Sawbones’ debt and convince him the only way to escape his pursuers is to board a ship bound for the eastern continent, far out of their reach. He is reluctant, but eventually agrees when you remind him what unknown adventures await in the land across the ocean. You see him off in the night and desperately hope that is the last you hear of this situation.

You are trying to enjoy a relaxing drink in the Tavern when a number of large men and Inox burst in and approach your table.

“So, you must be that little creep’s collateral,” one of the Inox says. “We’re here to collect.”

When you stare at her in silence, she tries again. “Little grey-bearded man. Wore symbols of the Great Oak. He said you lot would pay off his debt if he couldn’t.”

She pats an axe at her side. “Now, seeing as how he apparently skipped town, you can pay us, or things are gonna get ugly.”
You sigh and hand over the Sawbones’ debt, plus interest. Though it feels terrible, the thugs are satisfied and walk out the same way they came in. At least it is over now.
Refuse to pay. You won’t be strongarmed by anyone.

You laugh and wave your hand dismissively. There’s no way you will be paying such a large amount of money to these thugs. Unfortunately, the Inox is not amused.\n\n“Then your payment will be blood!” she says. “Meet us in the back alley, and we’ll see if we can’t come to terms.”

Followers of the Oak are religious healers who do their best to ward off the pestilence and death that can manifest in larger human cities. Contrary to popular belief, however, there is nothing miraculous about their healing methods, as anyone who has come to them with a gangrenous leg knows all too well. The mystique of the profession can get lost amongst the screams when the Sawbones has to hack off a limb.

Role: Melee Damage/Support Difficulty: Low Some of your abilities give a Medical Pack card to yourself or an ally. It goes into that character's hand, and they can play it on their turn to heal themselves. Hand them out before the fight gets rough. You are the party's doctor: strong heals that often also remove every negative condition, and cards that keep allies ed or immune to conditions for a while. Triage lets you heal a little every turn on top of your other actions. Your few attacks are nasty: they can , , , or , and a couple of them kill an enemy outright when it is already in bad shape. Strengths: • Particularly efficient healer • Has a number of decent melee attacks • Medical Packs can also increase Ally's card counts Weaknesses: • Poor ranged attacks • Weaker in parties with fewer allies or lower max health • Doesn't have as great an understanding of medical cleanliness as most doctors
Kill at least six enemies that are adjacent to at least one of your allies
Kill at least six enemies that are adjacent to none of your allies

Nobody sees the Scoundrel leave. You find out the way you were always going to find out: her bunk is stripped, the lock on the Trading Post's back door has been picked and relocked out of sheer habit, and on your table sits a small, neat pile of everything she ever lifted from you. A coin purse. A whetstone. The good knife.
There is a note under the knife, in handwriting far better than she ever let on. "Nothing personal. It never was. Thanks for the company; it was more than I came for."
The guard at the gate swears he saw nothing all night. He is probably telling the truth. She was always better than the people watching for her.
Weeks later a caravan master mentions a woman in dark leather who paid her way south and spent the whole trip teaching the drivers to cheat at cards. You find you are smiling. Somewhere out there, the Scoundrel is doing fine.

“You there! Stop!”

You turn to see a town guard walking briskly toward you.

“You are known associates of this woman, yes?” He holds up a crude sketch of the Scoundrel. “We believe she is behind a number of high-profile robberies and demand that you give us any information you have on her whereabouts and activities.”

His face softens a bit. “Look, I know you do a lot of good for the outpost, but the merchants are breathing down my neck on this one, and I could really use a lead.”
Cooperate with the guard and tell him everything you know.

The guard taps his notes with a smile on his face.\n\n“This is great,” he says. “I understand that you haven’t seen her in a while, but the information you’ve provided should still be useful. Have a nice day!”
Be as vague and unhelpful as possible, giving no useful information.

The guard scratches his head and looks down at his notes.\n\n“Well, that wasn’t very helpful,” he sighs. “But thanks for your time, I guess. Let me know if you remember anything or get any new information.”

Riding up on horses, a band of dirty, rough men quickly overtake and surround your group. They look hard and dangerous, and you immediately pull out your weapons as they approach.

Then you hear a familiar laugh.

“Well, if it isn’t my old crew.” A woman in dark leather armor leaps off her horse to come greet you. “You know what, boys? This lot gets a pass.”

She winks at you and turns around. “Plus, they’d probably kill you all if things turned ugly.”

Jumping back onto her horse, the Scoundrel looks back at you. “Well, it was nice seeing you. Just remember—you never saw me.”
Attack. Friend or not, those who prey on the weak should be brought to justice.

You see the bandits relax a little and begin to form up. That is when you strike. Some are scared off by the sudden attack, but others engage you hungrily. The Scoundrel throws a few good daggers, too, before she rides off, criticizing your poor decision-making.
The bandits seem a little disappointed as they form up and ride off in the opposite direction.

“So, I hear you stood up for me with the guards the other day. Such annoying pests, aren’t they?”

You turn around in the street to see the Scoundrel emerge from a dark alley with a smile on her face.

“I just wanted to thank you in person,” she says. “I’ve known quite a few persons who would have ratted me out for their chance at a piece of gold. It’s good to know some friendships last.”

She looks over her shoulder. “Listen, I’m leaving town for a good long while. You wanna grab a drink before I take off?”
Have a drink and reminisce about old times.

You laugh for a while and trade tales. As the sun drops below the tavern windows, the Scoundrel gets up to leave.

“Listen, I really did enjoy our time together, and, well, I just wanted to leave you with something to remember me by.”

A piece of black cloth flutters down onto the table. When you look back up, the Scoundrel is gone.
Overpower the Scoundrel and deliver her to the guards.

A look of horrid surprise flashes in the Scoundrel’s eyes as you leap forward and throw her to the ground. She doesn’t even speak as you bind her arms and take her to the guard. They thank you for your service, but their words aren’t much counter to the cold, angry stare of the Scoundrel as she’s taken away.

Role: Melee Damage Difficulty: Low Position is everything for you. Many of your attacks grow stronger when the target is next to one of your allies, and others when the target stands alone with no allies of its own nearby. Look at where your friends are before you pick a target, and work with them to flank enemies. You can also become , and some attacks, like Smoke Bomb, hit harder while you are unseen. Your attacks often add and , and poisoned enemies take extra damage from several of your cards. You move far and loot well, but you are fragile, with little to protect yourself. Strike and step away. Strengths: • High mobility • Potential for high melee Damage • Can afflict enemies with Poison Weaknesses: • Little in the way of effects that assist teammates • Few defensive abilities and low health • Will try and take ALL the gold
At the end of each scenario, each character in that scenario gains 8 experience if you successfully completed your battle goal
On your first turn of the scenario and the turn after each of your rests, perform one Song action that you have not yet performed this scenario
Have all 10 monster <sprite name=Curse> cards and all 10 <sprite name=Bless> cards in modifier decks at the same time

The last song is in the Tavern, which is where all of them were, and the whole outpost is there to hear it. The Soothsinger plays it twice: once the way she played it on the ice, fast and hard, the one that put spine into the guard when the Algox came over the wall, and once slowly, so that everyone can learn the words.
They do. By the end of the week the lumber crews are singing it on the road and getting it wrong, which she says is the point. "A song you have to be told is a song you forget," she tells you, packing the lute with the care other people give to children. "A song you get wrong is yours."
She is going south with the merchants, to the Capital, where there are halls with proper ceilings and audiences who have never heard what a Quatryl can do with eight strings and a grudge. She expects to be rich by midsummer. Knowing her, she will be.
The Tavern keeps the song. It is the one they play when the walls hold, and it is still, years on, slightly wrong.

Posters spring up in town announcing the performance of a master Quatryl musician and her merry band of performers. Looking closely at the image, you’re pretty sure you recognize that foppish feathered hat.\n\nThe poster says the next show is tonight. You decide to attend for one purpose or another.
Go to the show and cheer on the Soothsinger.
You go and enjoy the Soothsinger’s concert immensely. There is even a song or two about your party and its adventures around Gloomhaven.
Seems like a good opportunity to pick some pockets while people are distracted.
You put forth a valiant effort, but, due to a lack of skill, you don’t make much headway parting people from their money. At least the music is good.

Deep inside a dense forest, you begin to hear the jangling of bells and see a small troupe of performers approaching you through the trees.

“Well, look who it is!” The small voice belongs to a garishly dressed female Quatryl with a lute and a feathered hat. “Fancy running into you out here.” 

“This actually may be a stroke of luck,” the Soothsinger says. “You see, my compatriots and I seem to be a bit lost. We were headed toward the Capital when my drummer said he knew a shortcut. Now here we are in the middle of a forest without an inkling of a clue. I don’t suppose you could find it in your heart to escort us back to the main road, could you?"
Take the time to escort the troupe back out of the forest.

While escorting the Soothsinger and her troupe out of the forest, you are able to catch up a bit. She is very happy now as a traveling performer, playing to sold-out concerts across the land. When you reach the main road, you say your good-byes and then make the long trek back to where you were going.
Give detailed directions about the way out and hope that is sufficient.
You hem and haw and then give some vague directions back to the road. The Soothsinger looks at you skeptically and heads off.

Quatryls are not only master Engineers, but their impressive manual dexterity allows them to also become excellent Bards. These "Soothsingers" are able to empower their allies to great feats and bring their enemies low with a single strum of their lute. Their Song system works in a similar way to the Mindthief's Augments, and she is especially powerful in larger parties, but has low damage output.

Role: Ranged Support Difficulty: High You play songs. A song is a lasting card that helps every ally while it plays: more attack or range, healing each turn, , or making every enemy attack at disadvantage. Only one song plays at a time; playing a new one ends the old, unless a card lets you sing two at once. Your other cards work at range on whole groups: you , , and enemies, allies, and command allies to attack or move on your turn. Your own attacks are weak, so stay out of reach and let your party do the hitting. Strengths: • Wide range of powerful buffs • Varied selection of lower half abilities • Effective at crowd control Weaknesses: • Poor damage dealer • Weaker in smaller parties • Dubious fashion sense
Whenever you short rest, if Reviving Ether is in your discard pile, first return it to your hand
Infuse and consume all six elements
Perform four different loss actions twice each

The Spellweaver has been counting. You noticed it weeks ago: a small tally on the inside of her sleeve, a mark for every time Reviving Ether brought her cards back from the fire. "Thirty-one," she says, when you finally ask. "The sages say the ether forgives you nine times. After that, you are borrowing."
She is going home to the Orchid groves to pay it back, which as far as you can tell means sitting very still for a very long time. She does not seem to mind. "I have been loud enough," she says, and for a woman who once set a frozen lake on fire from the far shore, it is true.
Before she goes she walks the Alchemist's garden with the keeper, touching each bed in turn. Nothing visible happens. The following spring the garden comes up a week early and nobody can say why.
She leaves on foot, south, with a single staff and no coat, because the cold has never once been allowed to touch her and she sees no reason to start now.

In the very early morning, you are wakened by a knock at your door. Standing behind it is giant, dirty Inox wearing a leather apron.

“Oh, uh...ahem,” he coughs. “Sorry, I was looking for a female Orchid. She used to help me on occasion with my forge. Her control over fire was astounding and I paid her well for her assistance completing some of my specialty work.”

He scratches his head. “I guess she’s not around anymore. You wouldn’t happen to know where I could find someone who could help me in her absence, would you?”
Offer to help the blacksmith yourself.
The Inox is completely dumbfounded when you walk all the way down to his forge and then proceed to exhibit zero aptitude at manipulating or controlling fire.
Direct him to the Savvas Elemental Guild and go back to sleep.
“Ah, yes, that is probably a good idea,” he says. “Thanks for your time and I hope your friend the Spellweaver is doing well!”

Due to a late start, night falls before you can get to where you are going. You are on your guard throughout the night, but nothing can quite prepare you for a Night Demon attack.

They come upon you silent and invisible, so you are unaware of their presence until their claws sink into your flesh.
