The darkness erupts into chaos with flashing swords and horrific shrieks. And then a bolt of fire streaks through the darkness and incinerates one of the demons.

Someone else is out there.
Renew your efforts to slay the demons.

With the help of the mysterious firecaster, the battle turns and the demons are slain without much pain. Out of the darkness steps the familiar face of a female Orchid.

“Sorry about that. I think they were looking for this.” The Spellweaver holds up a black censer. “It’s a good thing I ran into you, though. I could use your help.”

She draws out a crude map. “Meet me here as soon as you can, and I’ll explain more.”
Use the distraction to disengage from the demons and run away.

This mysterious third party seems to have things under control, and the demons appear more interested in them anyway. You take the opportunity to retreat from the fight and run off into the night. You don’t feel great about it, but at least you’re alive.

Role: Ranged Damage Difficulty: High Your strongest spells are lost once you cast them. Reviving Ether brings every lost card back into your hand, so you can cast them all again; time it well, since it is lost too. You use every element. Create them with your spells, then spend them for stronger attacks, , , extra healing, or invisibility. Most of your attacks are at range and many hit whole areas. You are fragile, so stay back and let your spells do the work. Strengths: • Good ranged damage dealing • Can recover Burned cards with Reviving Ether • Access to decent early ranged summon Weaknesses: • Low health, can die very fast • Requires complex Ability management for new Players • Crystal skin makes it difficult to find a good tailor
Once each scenario, during ordering of initiative, after all ability cards have been revealed, all your summons gain <sprite name=Invisible>
Summon the Lava Golem on your first turn and keep it alive for the entire scenario
Perform the summon action of five different ability cards

The Summoner has been bringing things through from the other side for as long as you have known her, and sending them back when they were done, and you had assumed the arithmetic came out even. It does not, she tells you, on the last night, sitting at the Alchemist's bench with the black unicorn asleep across the doorway. "Every crossing costs the crosser. The planes keep the change."
She is thinner than she was. The Aesther are hard to read, but even you can see that.
"I am going to stop," she says, "somewhere the boundary is thick and nothing can hear me call." She has a place in mind, inland, where the ground is old and does not remember magic. She will not say where.
The unicorn goes back first, in the yard at dawn, unmade in a scatter of light that the children of the outpost talk about for the rest of their lives. Then the lava golem, then the sprite. Then the Summoner walks out of the gate on her own two feet, alone for the first time in years, and does not look as if she minds.

“A monstrous creature approaches the walls!” A guard with a truly terrified look runs toward you, waving his arms with manic energy. “Please! You must help!” Before you can even agree, he grabs you by the wrist and pulls you toward the East Gate.

You hear the beast before you see it, bellowing with rage and pounding at the gates. Each time it hits, the entire city shakes. You climb the ramparts and look down at the massive creature with six legs as thick as trees, two spiraling horns, and a spiked tail.

“This is truly a demon from the abyss,” the guard laments. It must be from another plane, so he’s not too far off.
Attack the beast from the wall, shooting arrows at it until it stops moving.

You grab a bow and start sending arrows down into the thing’s thick hide. Each individual arrow doesn’t do much, but over time the creature slows. By the time it manages to break through the gate, it has been considerably hobbled as black blood pours from its countless wounds. It charges forward, laying waste to a small shop, but as more arrows continue to rain down upon it, it soon stops and falls over lifeless.
Work on reinforcing the walls. Hold it off for as long as possible.

You set to work reinforcing the gate with anything you can find—planks of wood, carts full of stones, your own bodies. Due to your tremendous effort, the guards on the walls manage to bring down the beast before it breaks through. The various merchants of the Boiler’s District thank you for your valiant service.

Up ahead of you, you see a staff stuck in the very center of the road, pointing straight up out of the ground. You get closer, and an odd sense of foreboding comes over you.

You recognize the staff as the one wielded by the Summoner. The fact that it now in front of you with such a strange and ominous placement makes you very wary.

You quickly look around, but nothing else of note is in sight.
Take the staff and move on.

You shrug and grab the staff, half expecting something exciting to happen when you do. Instead, nothing happens at all. In fact, the staff seems rather mundane. You feel no power running through it at all. Still, no sense in leaving it behind. It could be important.
Investigate the area and get to the bottom of this.

You spend a good hour looking over the area, scouring every bush and divot you can find. Unfortunately, you find no other clues about what happened here and end up just tiring yourself out.\n\nYou shrug and grab the staff, half expecting something exciting to happen when you do. Instead, nothing happens at all. In fact, the staff seems rather mundane. You feel no power running through it at all. Still, no sense in leaving it behind. It could be important.

With the proper concentration, an Aesther Summoner can pull anything she wishes across the planar boundaries. With infinite planes comes infinite possibilities. Such efforts can be incredibly taxing, however, and a Summoner finds it much easier to transport living things or raw energy.

Role: Summoner/Support Difficulty: Medium You fight through your summons. Most of your cards call a creature to fight beside you, and the rest protect them, heal them, or let them act on your turn. Summons stay until they are defeated; some cards let you bring lost summon cards back. Your own attacks are modest and mostly at range, adding , , or when you spend , or . Spread your summons around the enemies and let them take the hits while you stay back. Strengths: • Wide array of creatures to summon • Support abilities for all allies • Reasonable ranged abilities Weaknesses: • Low damage dealing capacity • Too many active summons can leave too few cards • Expensive to make all the art for in a computer game!
Reduce attacks targeting you by a total of <sprite name=Shield> 20 or more in a single round
Infuse or consume <sprite name=CreateLight> during each of your turns

The Sunkeeper asks you to meet her on the wall at sunrise. She is already there when you arrive, armor polished to a mirror, watching the light come up over the ice. "The temple has sent for me," she says. "They need a keeper, and there is no one else."
She does not pretend to be sorry to go, and you respect her for it. Instead she walks the length of the wall with you, laying a gloved hand on each tower as she passes, speaking a few words under her breath. The guards on duty stand a little straighter without quite knowing why.
At the gate she presses a small sun medallion into your palm, warm from her hand. "For the dark months. It will not do much. It will do enough."
Then she turns south and walks into the sunrise, which is exactly how she would have wanted it to look.

You are haggling over the price of road rations with an irritating Valrath merchant when a messenger boy approaches you holding a note.

“Sir, I have a pressing letter from an important Valrath Sunkeeper,” the messenger says. “I was told to deliver it to you.”

You reach for it, but the messenger moves back a little. “Sir, this note has traveled a long distance to get to you. If you could, please pay a small fee to take possession of it.”

You throw the kid a few coins and grab the note. Enclosed with the note is a small medallion engraved with the image of the sun. Apparently the Sunkeeper thinks the object may help you at some point in the future. The note doesn’t say exactly how and the thing has no apparent use. You stow it away in your pack.
Refuse to pay for the note.

You laugh in indignation and push the messenger away. He opens his mouth to object, then thinks better of it and runs off. You turn back to bartering, now leveraging the proof of your extreme thriftiness against the merchant.

You see them long before they get close to you—radiant balls of light blazing against the horizon.

Sun Demons.

As they approach, you prepare for an attack, but the demons have other plans. They menace you with their glowing claws, but they would rather have information than kill you.

“Where is the one you call a Sunkeeper?” one of them hisses. “The Valrath neglects her duties, and now we must resolve matters personally.”

You press for further information, but the demons get angry. “These are not your concerns! Tell us where she is or die at our hands!”
Give them whatever information you can on the Sunkeeper’s whereabouts.

You’re not sure exactly what happened to the Sunkeeper after she left the party, but you tell the demons everything you know.\nThey seem satisfied with your response and even offer a bitter thanks as they fly off to the west.
Attack the demons. There are a lot of them, but you do not take kindly to threats.

Without even speaking, you draw your weapons and attack. The demons are caught off guard, but they bounce back with great ferocity. It is a long, brutal battle, and you continue on in your adventure greatly wounded and bloody.

You are heading through a small forest when you hear the sound of a woman screaming off to the west. You silently move closer, catching a glimpse of multiple radiant figures through the trees.

They are Sun Demons, perhaps the same ones who accosted you earlier. That suspicion is confirmed when you get closer and see they are hovering around an armored Valrath woman bound to a tree, torturing her for information.

“Don’t you see how important this is!” one of the demons says. “Give us the location of the temple!”

“Lies and tricks of a demon,” the Sunkeeper responds. “The temple is in no danger except from you.”
Leave the scene quietly and return to your own business.
Not wanting to get involved, you simply move on. Eventually the screams of the Sunkeeper fade away.
Attack the demons and free the Sunkeeper.

You charge out of the trees and attack the Sun Demons. Fueled by righteous indignation and a bit of guilt, you slay them all. The battle leaves you wounded, but the Sunkeeper happily mends your wounds once you free her.\n\n“They seemed to think the Sun Temple is under attack by Night Demons,” she says. “I have no reason to believe them, but still, would you mind helping me look into it?”

By now, the Sun Demons cut a very recognizable portrait against the horizon as they move toward you. You sincerely had hoped you were done with these creatures.

“We have urgent need of your assistance,” one of them starts. “Night Demons have infested the Sun Temple, attempting to desecrate it and send the world into eternal darkness.

“We have tried to stop them, but they are too fortified inside the temple. We regrettably need more strength.

“Please, you cannot want an absence of a sun on this plane any less than we do. It would be disastrous.”
Agree to help the Sun Demons.
You sigh and agree, warning them that this had better be the last time they ask you for a favor. They give you the location of the Sun Temple and implore you to hurry.
Attack the Sun Demons. It may be the only way to stop them from bothering you.

Without even speaking, you draw your weapons and attack. The demons are caught off guard, but they bounce back with great ferocity. It is a long, brutal battle, and you continue on in your adventure greatly wounded and bloody.

Sunkeepers have been trained to tap into long-dormant demonic powers and harness them for the purpose of righteousness. The Sunkeeper has an assortment of Healing, Buffing and Card Recovery abilities and is a capable Melee fighter in her own right. She works best in the role of a Paladin, aiding the main damage dealers in combat while keeping them alive.

Role: Melee Tank/Support Difficulty: Low Light is your fuel. Most of your cards create or spend it for stronger attacks, extra healing and longer buffs. Beacon of Light keeps Light glowing every turn. You lead from the front: several cards let an ally or on your turn, and your heals, and keep the party going. You also give allies and , and can take damage meant for them. You are tough and can with your own attacks, so stand next to your allies where you can protect and command them at the same time. Strengths: • Array of buff, heal and recovery options • Competent melee combatant • Uses Light to enhance her abilities Weaknesses: • Can struggle against groups of smaller enemies • Weaker with fewer allies • Rather self-righteous a lot of the time
Heal an ally or apply a negative condition to an enemy each turn
Perform two actions with lost icons before your first rest and then only rest after having played at least two actions with lost icons since your previous rest

The Tinkerer's workshop has taken over half the Craftsman's floor by the time he decides to leave it. Nobody argues; the Craftsman has been using his drill press for a month and has no intention of giving it back. "Keep it," the Tinkerer says. "Keep all of it. I am tired of carrying things."
He is going east, to look for the places the old maps mark and the new ones do not, with a bag of elixirs and one battle bot that follows him like a dog and has never once worked properly. He says the not-working is a feature. He has always said that.
The last thing he builds in Frosthaven is a lamp for the Infirmary that lights itself when someone comes in after dark, so the healers stop knocking over the tray of knives. It works the first time. He looks faintly disappointed.
A letter comes the next summer, smudged and full of diagrams. The Craftsman reads it twice and starts building something. He will not say what.

You return to your rooms for the evening to find a small note resting on the ground in front of your door.

It is from the Tinkerer, explaining that he has been pursuing further studies in flammable liquid delivery methods. He asks for your help in delivering to him a small robotic contraption that he absentmindedly left behind in a secret stash under the floorboards of his old room.

He details the device’s location and gives an address to deliver it to—some small village far to the northwest.
Oblige the Tinkerer and send along the contraption.

You don’t have the money to send him the contraption, so you decide just to keep it for yourself.\n\nLike an eager treasure hunter, you pry up the floorboards in the Tinkerer’s old room and find a trove of useless junk, plus a detailed robotic spider that is anything but useless. You switch it on and let it scurry around the room. This could be a significant help in battle. No way it’s getting shipped off.
You don’t want to pay for postage. Just keep the thing for yourself.

Like an eager treasure hunter, you pry up the floorboards in the Tinkerer’s old room and find a trove of useless junk, plus a detailed robotic spider that is anything but useless. You switch it on and let it scurry around the room. This could be a significant help in battle. No way it’s getting shipped off.

You probably wouldn’t have normally noticed it, but sometimes nature calls and you need to head off the beaten path to get some privacy.

Hidden in the bushes, you come across the smoking wreckage of some crude machine. It looks to have broken down at some point and was left here to rust and decay.

Most of it is scrap, but thanks to your time with the Tinkerer, you know a good power core when you see one. It’s a bit heavier than you’d hoped, but it should fetch a good price back in Gloomhaven.
The core sure is heavy. You manage it rather well, but it will be a bit of hindrance in battle. You hope the payoff is worth the trouble.
Leave the core alone. You don't want anything weighing you down in battle.

You decide the risk is not worth the reward and walk away from the contraption before you scratch yourself on the rusted metal and give yourself some foul disease. And just the thought of haggling with the Quatryls in the Mixed District about a fair price makes you tired and irritable.

Role: Ranged Support Difficulty: Medium You are the party's support from range. Your heals reach any ally within a few hexes, and other cards give allies their discarded or lost cards back, or even raise an ally's hand size. Your attacks are ranged and often hit areas, adding , or . You can also lay traps and mines, and summon gadgets like a decoy or a battlebot. Stay behind your allies: you are fragile, but you keep everyone else in the fight much longer. Strengths: • Decent ranged abilities • Effective healer • Wide range of options Weaknesses: • Very fragile • Weaker in smaller teams • Has trouble opening tight jars

Give at least one ally or enemy <sprite name=Poison>, <sprite name=Strengthen>, <sprite name=Bless>, or <sprite name=Ward> each round

The Voidwarden has been filling a jar with black sand. A pinch at a time, after every scenario, from wherever the Void touched the world through her and left its coarse, dark residue behind. The jar is nearly full. "That is the measure of it," she says, turning it in the light. "Everything I ever made disappear. It does not look like much."
She is going to the Capital, to the archives, to write down what she knows. "No one who touches the Void lives long enough to teach the next one. I intend to be the exception." She says it without drama; the scars down her left side say the rest.
She leaves the jar with the Alchemist, with a label in her small, exact hand: DO NOT OPEN. The Alchemist, who has opened everything else anyone ever left her, puts it on the highest shelf and does not touch it.
The morning the caravan goes, the sick in the Infirmary are quieter than usual, and the healers find every one of them a little better than the day before. Nobody saw her go in.

The Void is a dangerous and terrible place. Anything that enters it dissolves into a coarse, black sand without explanation or remorse. After a near-death experience with the Void as a child which scarred the left side of their body, the Voidwarden made it their duty to protect others from a similar fate. Being touched by the Void has left more than just physical scars however. They can channel the power behind the Void to manipulate the thoughts and actions of both allies and foes. The Voidwarden can also offer powerful boons of healing and stamina, but those gifts comes at a terrible price.

Instead you take control of enemies, making them move or attack their own allies for an action, and you command your allies to or on your turn. Your power has a price. Many of your heals and blessings also the ally you help, and some cards you unless you spend . Plan who you heal and when. You create and ; Ice makes your heals stronger. Your own few attacks pile on several conditions at once. Strengths: • Large starting hand size • Works better in larger parties • Wide array of bottom half abilities Weaknesses: • Generally slow character • Reasonably squishy • Complicated skincare regime
